caption: FTC v. Wyndham Worldwide Corp.
citation_line: FTC v. Wyndham Worldwide Corp., 10 F. Supp. 3d 602 (D.N.J. 2014), aff’d, 799 F.3d 236 (3d Cir. 2015)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Salas denied Wyndham’s motion to dismiss the FTC’s claim that allegedly unreasonable cybersecurity practices were “unfair” under § 5 of the FTC Act.
qualification_rationale: The ruling became a landmark in federal cybersecurity enforcement by confirming that the FTC may police inadequate corporate data-security practices under its unfairness authority; it received extensive national press coverage.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed in a precedential interlocutory opinion, holding that the FTC had statutory authority over cybersecurity and that Wyndham had fair notice of potential liability.
